title: Stress, Strain, Elasticity and Plasticity
notes: **Stress $\sigma$:** force per unit area. $\sigma = F/A$. Units: N/m$^2$ or Pa.
**Strain $\epsilon$:** fractional deformation. $\epsilon = \Delta L/L$. Strain is dimensionless.
**Elasticity:** the property of a material to return to its original shape and size after the deforming force is removed.
**Plasticity:** the property of a material to undergo permanent deformation without breaking. Beyond the elastic limit, materials become plastic.
**Types of stress:** tensile stress (stretching), compressive stress (squashing), and shear stress (sliding layers).
